name: Kaiserjägermuseum
kurzbeschreibung: The Kaiserjägermuseum on Bergisel explores the history of the Tyrolean Kaiserjäger and forms an ensemble with Das Tirol Panorama and its 1,000 m² giant cyclorama.
preis: Kombiticket Erwachsene 12,00 €, Ermäßigte 9,00 €, unter 19 Jahren frei
oeffnungszeiten: Mi–Mo 09:00–17:00 Uhr (Dienstag Ruhetag; letzter Einlass 16:30 Uhr)
beschreibung:
Overview

The venerable Kaiserjägermuseum is perched on the steeped-in-history Bergisel in the south of the Tyrolean state capital Innsbruck at around 750 metres above sea level. Founded in 1880, it ranks among the oldest military museums in the world. Together with the museum Das Tirol Panorama, which opened in 2011, it forms a unique cultural and historical ensemble. The museum is dedicated to the more than century-long history of the four Tiroler Kaiserjäger-Regimenter of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy, using countless original exhibits to illustrate everyday military life, identity, and the tragic fates of Tyrolean soldiers in high-alpine warfare.

Collections, Giant Cyclorama & History

The Kaiserjäger were established in 1816 by Emperor Franz I. von Österreich and were recruited almost exclusively from Tirol and Vorarlberg. The museum houses an invaluable collection of historical artifacts: original dress and field uniforms, weapons, banners, paintings, historic photographs, and personal diaries document the campaigns in Italy (1848/1859), the Battle of Custozza (1866), right through to the dramatic mountain warfare along the Dolomite and Isonzofront in the First World War (1915–1918). The centrepiece of the complex is the underground-connected museum Das Tirol Panorama: here, visitors encounter the monumental Innsbrucker Riesenrundgemälde, covering over 1,000 m². Created in 1896 by Munich painter Michael Zeno Diemer and his assistants, the 360-degree panoramic masterpiece draws viewers right into the midst of the third Battle of Bergisel on 13 August 1809, in which Tyrolean riflemen led by Andreas Hofer fought against Bavarian and French troops.

Visit & Getting There

The Kaiserjägermuseum and Das Tirol Panorama are open from Wednesday to Monday from 09:00 to 17:00 (closed on Tuesdays; last admission 16:30). Admission prices (as of 2025/2026): combined ticket for Das Tirol Panorama with Kaiserjägermuseum €12.00 for adults, €9.00 for seniors and students, free for children and youths under 19! Admission is completely free with the all-inclusive Innsbruck Card. By public transport: from Innsbrucker Hauptbahnhof, take tram line 1 or the Stubaitalbahn (STB) to the Bergisel stop (approx. an 8-minute uphill walk) or conveniently take the Sightseer bus line directly to the museum entrance. By car: Brennerautobahn A13 (exit Innsbruck Süd) or A12 (exit Innsbruck Mitte); pay-and-display parking spaces are available on Bergiselweg.

Tips

The modern building of Das Tirol Panorama is completely accessible with lifts and stepless entrances; the historic Kaiserjägermuseum can be reached step-free via an underground connecting corridor suitable for wheelchairs. The panoramic terrace of the adjacent restaurant 1809 offers a marvelous view of the city of Innsbruck and the Nordkette.
